notes: Works on both backends with consistent lookup, but special-cases out-of-range seeks for zip symlinks inside the generic Open path, and the squashfs NewObject/root fallback logic is convoluted.

Correct translation in both backends, with root and NewObject suffix handling that agree with List, but the zip Open special-casing for an offset past the end is awkward and a symlink/regular .rclonelink name clash is not handled.
Identical to C3: matches the reference code exactly, with docs and adequate tests.
Code is identical to the reference fix and is minimal and correct; tests cover listing, reading and escape but not range/seek or lookup by the unsuffixed name.

Functional, with tie-breaking where a regular .rclonelink member wins over a symlink, but it patches dirtree slices by index and uses an empty target to mean 'not a link', so empty-target symlinks are hidden.
Works and tests thoroughly, but squashfs uses an empty link target as the is-a-symlink marker (so empty-target symlinks are mishandled), and the zip clash handling patches dirtree slices by index.
Handles regular-vs-symlink clashes and roots named either way, but changing newObjectNative to return *Object means NewObject can return a typed-nil interface, and the zip root logic is fiddly.

Solid implementation where regular .rclonelink members win over clashing symlinks in both backends and a root can name a symlink either way; minor nit is that clashing symlinks are not counted in the skip notice.

Rewrites readZip heavily and silently hides members inside symlinks (failing the escape test); it also adds unrequested behaviour: an ErrLinkNeedsSuffix error and changing a non-dir squashfs root into ErrorDirNotFound.

Symlink exposure works, but the hostile-archive defence is a heavy readZip rewrite that silently drops members inside a symlink, so the copy no longer errors and the hidden escape test fails; it also makes an unrelated squashfs List error change and adds a new shared package.
Close to the reference with a clean squashfs lookup (regular name first, then suffix fallback), and thorough tests including notice, range/seek, root and escape.

Clean implementation with a find helper that keeps NewObject consistent with List, plus thorough tests including the skip notice, range/seek and a single-object root; no clash handling, same as the reference.
Correct and close to the reference, with a slightly redundant double remote check in NewObject; one test leaves the global logger set to discard.
Close to the reference with sensible suffixed-root and NewObject name checks; it has a redundant double Remote check and no regular-vs-symlink clash handling, which the reference also lacks.
Code is identical to the reference, plus docs and reasonable zip, squashfs and escape tests; it lacks range/seek and log-notice coverage.
Identical to C8 and the reference: minimal and correct, with modest tests that lack range/seek and name-agreement checks.

Adds a case-insensitive LinkFilter that drops symlinks and even regular .rclonelink members (contrary to the spec) and fails the escape test; squashfs NewObject now builds the whole directory's entries on every lookup.

The case-insensitive LinkFilter drops a symlink that has members beneath it (failing the hidden escape test) and can also drop regular .rclonelink members, contrary to the spec, at the cost of significant extra machinery.

Both backends work with --links, but the zip side reads every symlink target eagerly and silently drops symlinks that clash with other entries; that keeps writes inside the destination but diverges from the expected behaviour (the copy errors) and fails the hidden escape test.
Core feature is fine, but zip addLinks drops symlinks that have entries inside them (failing the hidden escape test) and mutates the dirtree by inserting nil directory keys, which is hacky.
